name: Galileo’s accelerated-motion analysis
description: Mathematical laws of uniformly accelerated falling motion.

impact.note: New mathematical account of fall and projectiles for natural philosophers; kinematics and Newtonian dynamics built on it, but the platform is credited to later mechanics.

date.basis: Year of the source-bounded episode, not necessarily invention.

events.statement: Galileo’s Two New Sciences presented a mathematical treatment of accelerated motion, including the relation between distance and elapsed time.

evidence.supports: The translation sets out the accelerated-motion theorems.
Dates the Leiden first edition to 1638.

contributions.resource: Developed or authored the described account.

evidence.supports: The translation sets out the accelerated-motion theorems.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest dated source-bounded episode in this record, not a claim of worldwide priority.

caveats: Publication follows earlier work and is not the first study of falling motion. The text presents idealized acceleration and reports measurements; it is not evidence for an exact modern vacuum test or Newton’s later force law.

research.note: Chronology distinguishes composition or formulation from later surviving textual witnesses. Independent review checked the event dating and scope against the cited work, historical source, edition metadata or modern translation, as applicable.
